programme.desc: Ball-coise bhon dàrna ìre den SWPL le Cill Mhearnaig a’ cluich an aghaidh Boroughmuir. Aithris bho Calum Dòmhnallach. Football action from the second tier of the SWPL as Kilmarnock face Boroughmuir. Commentary comes from Calum MacDonald.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air càil ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha Kylie Wylie trang a' rèiteach ghruagan. The colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. Hairdresser Kylie Wylie takes on a hair-raising professional challenge.

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Le feum fhathast air Bus Ghlaschu, sa phrògram mu dheireadh chi sinn gu bheil na ceanglaichean eadar Glaschu is Dùn nan Gall làidir is seasmhach. The Glasgow bus is still used widely today and we see how connections between Donegal and the city are still strong.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: Scottish Women's Premier League (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: Football action from the SWPL as Celtic welcome Hearts. Presented pitchside from New Douglas Park with Calum MacAulay, commentary comes from Derek Mackay. Ball-coise beò bho SWPL le Celtic a’ cur fàilte air Hearts. An geama slàn ri fhaicinn le Calum MacAmhlaidh a’ preasantadh bho oir na pàirce agus aithris bho Derek MacAoidh.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach seachdainn le sgioba-naidheachd BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Bidh Iain MacFhionghain a' tòiseachadh streath ùr de Alleluia le measgachadh de laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. Anns a’ chiad phrògram, bidh Iain a leughadh cosamhlachd agus cluinnear laoidhean freagarrach, feadhainn air an clàradh as ùr airson Alleluia. Am measg nan seinneadairean bidh Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ seinn An t-Seann Chladh Thall agus Dòmhnall-Iain MacIlleDhuinn a’ seinn Anns a’ Chrann. Bhon tasglann cluinnear Catrìona Watt a’ seinn Air Geugan Seilich. An t-seachdain-sa cluinnidh sinn leughaidhean agus smuaintean bhon t-Urr Daibhidh MacNeacail agus bho Kathleen Reddy agus bidh Iain fhèin cuideachd a’ leughadh earrann bho Chosamhlachdan. Iain MacKinnon reads a parable and introduces fitting hymns and psalms - some recorded especially for the programme. Eilidh Cormack performs An t-Seann Chladh Thall and Donald-Iain Brown sings Anns a’ Chrann. From the extensive Alleluia! archives, an opportunity to hear Catriona Watt singing Air Geugan Seilich. Rev David Nicolson and Kathleen Reddy each present their chosen reading from the Bible and related reflections. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod gathers seaweed from the shore to put into a cake and uses locally grown vegetables in a tart.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the ‘Pretenders’, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Seumas & Innes or Liz Anne & Eilidh, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Seumas & Innes no Liz Anne & Eilidh, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr?

programme.title: Chernobyl – Utopia na Smàl/Chernobyl – Utopia in Flames
programme.desc: Tha a’ chiad readhachtar niùclasach foillsichte san t-saoghal na chunnart dhan t-siostam Sobhieteach air fad. Ach, fiù ’s an dèidh dhaibh sgòth rèidio-beò a lorg os cionn an t-Suain, tha Mosgo a’ fuireach sàmhach. Tha e a’ toirt 36 uairean a thìde an dèidh na mòr-thubaist an riaghaltas innse do dhaoine gum feum iad baile Pripyat, a tha a-nis air a thruailleadh, fhàgail. The world's first exposed nuclear reactor is a danger to the entire Soviet system. However, even after the discovery of a radioactive cloud over Sweden, Moscow continues to remain silent. Then, 36 hours after the catastrophe, the Soviet government finally decides to evacuate the contaminated city of Pripyat. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Às dèidh toiseach tòiseachaidh dùbhlanach, lean Somhairle agus Innes orra a’ rothaireachd air a Bhadger Divide, far an tàinig iad tarsainn air duilgheadasan meacanaigeach; uisge trom; geàrr-rathaidean; tionndadh ceàrr agus bagannan caillte! Thàinig an rothaiche agus an neach-gleidhidh chlàran, Kerry Nic a’Phì, còmhla riutha airson earrann. After a tough start, Somhairle and Innes continue riding the Badger Divide, where they encounter mechanical issues, torrential rain, shortcuts, wrong turns and lost baggage! They’re joined for a section by record-holder, cyclist Kerry MacPhee.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2025 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Ímar, Larry Campbell & Teresa Williams, The East Pointers, Georgia Cécile agus Ainsley Hamill. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2025, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Ímar, Larry Campbell and Teresa Williams, The East Pointers, Georgia Cécile and Ainsley Hamill. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Ann an saoghal làn gleadhraich, ciamar a tha beathaichean a’ dèanamh ciall dheth? In a world filled with noise, how do animals make sense of it all?

programme.title: The Magic of Dance
programme.desc: Dance has almost always moved freely across frontiers. Just as in the 19th century, Italian and French dancers went to Russia to make their names, so in the 20th century, Diaghilev reversed the flow by bringing the Ballets Russes to live and work in Western Europe. All part of the ebb and flow of dance. Margot Fonteyn visits Tchaikovsky's house near Moscow and talks to Marie Rambert about Diaghilev. The programme includes unique film of Pavlova, as well as Mikhal Baryshnikov dancing Petrushka.

programme.title: Omnibus

programme.title: Dance Passion Swansea
programme.desc: Dancers of all kinds take over Swansea’s streets, landmarks, parks and beaches to showcase the city, explore what home means and celebrate the life-enhancing joy of dance. The performances feature solos, duets and ensembles across a variety of dance styles, including ballet, Latin, contemporary, ballroom, breaking, traditional clog and Welsh folk. Locations range from Mumbles Pier and skateboard park to Swansea Bay and the dunes, beaches and bays of the Gower peninsula.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: Talking Movies takes a look at some classic French cinema. France boasts one of the most successful and thriving film industries in Europe. Tom Brook and some fellow cineastes pick their favourite French films and tell the stories behind their creation, from 'Breathless', the movie that heralded the French New Wave, to 'Amélie', the film that shows Paris to perfection. These are all French films that broke new ground and as we hear from their fans, they feel as vibrant today as when they were first made.

programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, analyses the Iranian position in their confrontation with the United States in the Gulf, examines the state of play in Russia's war with Ukraine and looks at the chances of Benjamin Netanyahu surviving as Israeli prime minister after elections later this year.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Twenty years ago a man arriving for a job interview at BBC Television Centre was taken into a live TV studio and asked to comment on a legal story. The clip quickly spread on early video-sharing sites and became a meme. Guy Goma reflects on what happened, alongside Elliott Gotkine, the journalist involved in the original error. Saudi Arabia has spent large sums on sport and media in recent years, aiming to build influence as well as make financial returns. New developments, including changes to sports funding and involvement in major media deals, suggest a shift in approach. Claire Enders, founder of Enders Analysis, and Claire Atkinson, contributing editor at The Ankler and founder of Media Mix, outline how the strategy is changing. Climate change remains one of the most complex stories for news organisations to cover. It involves long-term change, scientific detail and questions about how to keep audiences engaged. David Shukman, journalist and former BBC Science Editor, sets out his view on how climate reporting has developed and the issues it faces.

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive heads for the east coast of Barbados to check out the world’s oldest rum distillery. He puts a shift in with the hens on an organic family farm that stretches out for over 100 acres, tests out his flexibility alongside British expats with some cliff-top yoga and finally meets a young Bajan spoken word poet at the Builders of Barbados wall.

programme.desc: Extended highlights of Celtic v Rangers as the race for the Scottish Premiership title hots up.

programme.title: Serie A Scots
programme.desc: Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay had an incredible first season in Italian football. Their Napoli side won the League and Super Cup, but perhaps their greatest achievement is yet to come with Scotland heading to World Cup 2026. Jonathan Sutherland returns to Napoli to meet the Scottish superstars of Serie A.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: The River Don rises in wild land, high on the moors of the Grampian mountains. Paul follows its easterly flow from the famous Cock Bridge, where he encounters the Lonach Highlanders and a clan chief with two feathers in his cap carrying relics of the Battle of Culloden. Close to Strathdon, Paul meets an artist and sculptor who creates lifelike creatures from scrap metal, and then learns how the Aberdeen Angus became a world-beating cattle breed. At Alford, he explores an unusual transport museum and hears about an eccentric and brilliant postman who invented a steam automobile. A trip in a vintage Rolls-Royce takes Paul further along the course of the river. At Kemnay, he visits the huge quarry that once provided granite for prestigious buildings across the UK. As the river nears the sea, Paul meets a woman who wove overcoats for the Red Army. He then helps a Bulgarian couple harvest honey from their black Scottish bees before reaching the mouth of the river on the North Sea coast.

programme.title: Debate Night
programme.desc: Stephen Jardine hosts a special programme analysing the results of the Scottish Parliament election. A studio audience in Edinburgh put their questions to a panel of politicians and public figures to explore what the result means for Scotland.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Winston receives wounding news about his remaining leg. Meanwhile, Isa struggles with her new cleaning job at the undertaker’s, and Tam pushes his skinflintishness to new depths.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Traffic officers McKirdy and Singh fall out over issuing a ticket to a family member but make up over some music at the end of their shift. City cops McLaren and Fletcher meet a familiar face while attending a bag snatch, and rural officers Mackay and McIntosh deal with some quarrelsome landowners. Call Centre Operator Maggie LeBeau has some useful advice for homebuyers, Sergeant Karen Ann Millar has to deal with a curry pie and a birthday cake, and Volunteer Officer Beattie finds himself following the leads of five dogs. The Chief explains the importance of listening to the public and the implausibility of some people's names, before heading to London for a press conference to launch a combined Scottish Police Force/London City Force initiative with an old colleague.

programme.title: Karen Dunbar Live from Ayr
programme.desc: Join Karen Dunbar for an amazing night of side-splitting comedy. Karen is one of Scotland’s most recognisable comedy performers ever, from her breakthrough on Chewin’ the Fat to her success with The Karen Dunbar Show. Her stage career spans everything from Glasgow pantomime to London’s West End, and now she is taking on stand-up comedy in her hometown. This year has seen Karen out on the road with her brand new show, and she is bringing it back to Ayr for one more sold-out night. From delving through her experiences growing up in the 80s to hosting wild karaoke nights in Glasgow in her 20s and revisiting some of her favourite characters, this is Karen like you’ve never quite seen her before.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: Louise is distressed to learn she's carrying a girl, not a boy. After Donna fires Tim, she is forced to work with depressed Janet and mad Munch. Gaz struggles to train Munch to be his best man, while Janet picks a theme for Donna and Gaz's wedding: 'dead Jonny'.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: Gaz works through his list of three things he must do before he dies. Donna gets work in a charity shop to try to overcome her fear of death. Louise stumbles across a massive secret about Corinthian.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: When the bailiffs come to repossess her house, Janet has just 24 hours to get some money or lose her home. Louise finds a rich criminal who seems keen to help but all he offers Janet is a spit roast. Gaz struggles to babysit his son Corinthian. Donna desperately awaits the call to an interview for her dream job.

programme.title: Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps
programme.desc: When Donna goes to London to get her dream job, Janet and Gaz are left alone together. After a night of Lambrini and candles they wake up and realise they've had sex again. Donna learns the art of bluff during her interview. Louise starts having contractions.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda has spent most of her life avoiding being set up by her mother Penny. Old school pal Tilly sets her up on a blind date with an army doctor friend, Dreamboat Charlie. The date doesn't go quite to plan and so Penny insists on throwing a party to introduce Miranda to a suitable man. Miranda is notoriously bad at coming up with excuses, but when she sees a photo of her intended date he is so bad that the only option left is to lie and come out to her mother in an attempt to stop her from matchmaking.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: When a handsome man leaves his wallet in the shop, Miranda and Stevie think it could be a sign, especially when they discover he's called Robert Husband. They become highly competitive and try to find out who he'd prefer to take to dinner if he had to choose one of them. Meanwhile, Tilly has invited Miranda to Henley Regatta under the strict proviso that she doesn't embarrass her. Miranda is determined to be able to cope at a tricky social occasion just once. Old friend Gary seems to be the only person who believes Miranda should just be herself. Gary, meanwhile, has been offered a new job in Hong Kong, but seems to be waiting for someone to persuade him to stay; will Miranda take the hint?

During the First World War, two soldiers are ordered across no-man's-land and deep into enemy territory to deliver a message. If they fail, an entire battalion, under the mistaken belief the Germans are retreating, will be ordered over the top and into a deadly trap.

programme.title: James Arthur: Out of Our Minds
programme.desc: Multi-platinum-selling singer-songwriter James Arthur is at a crossroads in his life. After being propelled to stardom following his X Factor win in 2012, it has been a decade of highs but also desperate lows. James suffers from anxiety, depression and severe panic attacks. At his worst, he has considered taking his own life. Now 34, he is wondering if returning to the anti-depressants he has rejected might finally give him peace of mind. This documentary follows James as he explores the roots of his fragile mental health and searches for ways to cope.

programme.title: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
programme.desc: On a daily basis, Roman Kemp is contacted by young people who are struggling. With people turning to him for advice, he’s questioning whether or not there is a worsening mental health crisis and asking if these young people should be offered more support in their own communities. This documentary follows Roman as he immerses himself in schools, youth centres and treatment settings around the country, meets with experts and charities, and visits the Houses of Parliament to try to understand the potential solutions for improving the mental health of young people in the UK today.

programme.title: Charlie Cooper’s Myth Country
programme.desc: Charlie Cooper, who wrote and starred in the BBC’s This Country, has a fascination for the weird and wonderful world of British folklore. In this episode, with the help of an old AA van, he goes in search of Black Shuck, the demon dog of East Anglia. Despite a local legend that seeing Shuck brings with it a curse, Charlie meets locals who claim they have survived such encounters. Keen to capture the beast on camera, he attempts an overnight stakeout, with unexpected consequences. Alleged sightings of this 900-year-old hell hound are recorded almost monthly, so is Charlie in with a chance? His humorous odyssey takes him across Norfolk and Suffolk, where he meets witnesses and learns that in Britain almost every county has its own mythical creature. You only need to scratch the surface anywhere in this land to discover that folklore, myth and legend are very much alive.

programme.title: Margrete: Queen of the North
programme.desc: Powerful and tense historical epic about the untold story of the woman who united Scandinavia in a time of war. The year is 1402. Margrete has achieved what no man has managed before: she has gathered Denmark, Norway and Sweden into a peace-oriented union that she rules through her adopted son, King Erik. But a conspiracy is in the making, and Margrete finds herself in an impossible dilemma that could shatter her life’s work.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Reeling from a sudden loss, Shannon lashes out at her family. Only Ollie can offer her some comfort in the form of a dodgy vape. When Shannon’s day takes a surreal turn, she reconnects with herself and confronts her fears. But Dylan’s return snaps her back into a painful reality.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Dylan’s new life brings moments of comfort, but he also finds it challenging in a way he never saw coming. His old coping mechanisms no longer work, and he’s forced to ask himself what he truly wants. A conversation with Luke reminds him what’s at stake and what actually matters. Meanwhile, Cat seeks clarity from her son, hoping to understand the future she wants for herself and her family.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Take a Hike
programme.desc: This week, we’re in the Highlands and Islands of Scotland with nearly 5,000 km of coast. It’s home to five keen walkers, all determined to get their hands on the prize. Last to lead a walk is 32-year-old Rob from Dundee, who works for a communications company and plays amputee football for Partick Thistle. So what’s he got planned to win the golden walking stick? He’s leading the walkers to one of the Highland’s best-known spots. Glenfinnan Viaduct has been made famous the world over as the location that the Hogwarts Express steamed through in the Harry Potter movies. Will the infamous Scottish wet weather dampen the spirits and scotch Rob’s chances of winning?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads for Ben Ledi in the Trossachs to help with some high-altitude fieldwork. And 25 years on from the foot-and-mouth outbreak, Arlene finds out about a legacy that is helping today's farmers. Elsewhere, Rosie is in Gairloch Wester Ross to hunt for herring and find out how this over-exploited species is making a comeback. Leanna is in Fife, where she joins a team researching the movements of secretive snipe, and Cammy visits the Ayrshire couple determined to preserve and promote the Clydesdale horse breed.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Planting borders and planning for cut flowers are on Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham’s to-do list at the garden. Lizzie is direct sowing in the new cuttings area and Brian is in the zig-zag border, planting varieties that will grow tall, making them ideal for the back of a plot without requiring support or staking. Brian kicks off this year’s collection of plants being cultivated in the 6x8ft glasshouse. This is the most common-sized domestic greenhouse, so if you are lucky enough to have one, Brian has some great ideas for this season. Lizzie is the first of the presenters to start work in her competition plot. The theme this year is planting that will appeal to one of the senses, and Lizzie has one of the most challenging: touch. Plus, there is a report on the alpine collection at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, and all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Big Zuu brings big flavours and big energy to the studio with his super malt ribs with a fiery jalapeno coleslaw and spiced suya potatoes. Sophie Wyburd whips up a brilliant mid-week Greek-style dinner with her pork and halloumi koftas, quick homemade flatbreads and an olive and cabbage salad. Tony Singh makes a delicious brunch, folding masala spices through scrambled eggs served with buttered asparagus and topped with port-glazed lobster. Helen McGinn has some top alternatives to wine, while Samin Nosrat shares her recipe for alphonso mango pie. Finally, Iain Stirling gets either his food heaven, halibut, or his food hell, prawns. Meanwhile, Rick Stein tucks into to some of the best Cumbrian produce, and Clive Myrie meets the Dominican Republic’s answer to Nigella Lawson.

programme.title: Best Bakes Ever
programme.desc: Actress and cake expert Jane Asher brings together a selection of recipes from the nation's favourite television chefs. Each episode gives baking fans another chance to experience classic dishes from the likes of the James Martin, Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, the Hairy Bikers, Raymond Blanc, Nigella Lawson, Tom Kerridge, Lorraine Pascale and Rachel Khoo. There's added insight and appreciation from Jane herself, too. Whether it's cakes, pies, puddings or main courses - this greatest hits of baking is a must for anyone with a need to knead, and should help inspire even more of us to start getting creative in the kitchen.

programme.title: Tea with Mussolini
programme.desc: Florence 1935. A circle of English ladies settled in the cultured city take an orphan boy, Luca, under their wing. programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Florida is famous for its beaches, blue water and year round sun – but it also has a surprising wild side. It is home to pine forests, coral reefs and the famous Everglades wetland, the largest sub-tropical wilderness in the US. Here, manatees swim in crystal clear rivers, baby alligators practice their hunting skills and miniature deer roam free. Every year, this state faces the full forces of nature - from wildfires to flooding and powerful hurricanes. And today, a growing human population and a cast of animal invaders are threatening this wild paradise. With the help of pioneering scientists, will Florida’s wildlife continue to weather the storm?

Tony Singh makes a delicious brunch, folding masala spices through scrambled eggs served with buttered asparagus and topped with port-glazed lobster. Helen McGinn has some top alternatives to wine, while Samin Nosrat shares her recipe for alphonso mango pie. Finally, Iain Stirling gets either his food heaven, halibut, or his food hell, prawns. programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his journey, Michael travels to South Korea’s south west, where food, protest and landscape reveal the values that have shaped the modern nation. Arriving by high-speed train in Gwangju, he explores the region’s deep-rooted food culture, meeting a prizewinning kimchi maker to learn how Korea’s iconic fermented dish has sustained communities for centuries and become a symbol of shared labour and tradition. Michael then confronts a darker chapter in South Korea’s history at the May 18th Memorial Park, where a survivor of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising recounts how student-led protests against military rule were brutally suppressed and why the events are now regarded as the cornerstone of Korean democracy. Leaving the mainland, Michael crosses by ferry to Jeju Island, a volcanic landscape dominated by Mount Halla. Exploring lava tubes with a volcanologist, he uncovers how the island was formed before meeting the Haenyeo, Jeju’s legendary female free divers.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: In 1995, at the start of the Silicon Valley tech boom, Elon arrives with his younger brother Kimbal to join the gold rush and be part of the creation of the internet. They’re geeky young South Africans battling to make a fortune, but Elon is still sleeping on the floor of his office and washing at the local YMCA. Burdened with student debt, Elon and his brother create their first company, which they go on to sell for millions. Within just four years, at the age of 28, Musk is a multi-millionaire. But on his honeymoon, things start to go wrong.

programme.title: Scandinavia with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The first leg of Simon’s Scandinavian journey takes him from Svalbard, the beautiful archipelago that marks the northernmost outpost of Norway, south into the magical snowy region of Lapland. In freezing conditions, he travels to Nato's longest border with Russia, where tensions are high and even Santa's village is prepared for a potential war.

programme.title: The Iron Claw
programme.desc: Based on the true story of the inseparable Von Erich brothers, who made history in the intensely competitive world of professional wrestling in the early 1980s.

programme.title: Surge
programme.desc: Airport security worker Joseph lives a mundane existence with a daily commute and a repetitive job. After a frustrating reunion with his unresponsive parents, he cracks under the pressure and embarks on a frenzy of emotional release.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Florida is famous for its beaches, blue water and year round sun – but it also has a surprising wild side. It is home to pine forests, coral reefs and the famous Everglades wetland, the largest sub-tropical wilderness in the US. Here, manatees swim in crystal clear rivers, baby alligators practice their hunting skills and miniature deer roam free. Every year, this state faces the full forces of nature - from wildfires to flooding and powerful hurricanes. And today, a growing human population and a cast of animal invaders are threatening this wild paradise. With the help of pioneering scientists, will Florida’s wildlife continue to weather the storm?

programme.title: Margrete: Queen of the North
programme.desc: Powerful and tense historical epic about the untold story of the woman who united Scandinavia in a time of war. The year is 1402. Margrete has achieved what no man has managed before: she has gathered Denmark, Norway and Sweden into a peace-oriented union that she rules through her adopted son, King Erik. But a conspiracy is in the making, and Margrete finds herself in an impossible dilemma that could shatter her life’s work.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Reeling from a sudden loss, Shannon lashes out at her family. Only Ollie can offer her some comfort in the form of a dodgy vape. When Shannon’s day takes a surreal turn, she reconnects with herself and confronts her fears. But Dylan’s return snaps her back into a painful reality.

programme.title: Mint
programme.desc: Dylan’s new life brings moments of comfort, but he also finds it challenging in a way he never saw coming. His old coping mechanisms no longer work, and he’s forced to ask himself what he truly wants. A conversation with Luke reminds him what’s at stake and what actually matters. Meanwhile, Cat seeks clarity from her son, hoping to understand the future she wants for herself and her family.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Take a Hike
programme.desc: This week, we’re in the Highlands and Islands of Scotland with nearly 5,000 km of coast. It’s home to five keen walkers, all determined to get their hands on the prize. Last to lead a walk is 32-year-old Rob from Dundee, who works for a communications company and plays amputee football for Partick Thistle. So what’s he got planned to win the golden walking stick? He’s leading the walkers to one of the Highland’s best-known spots. Glenfinnan Viaduct has been made famous the world over as the location that the Hogwarts Express steamed through in the Harry Potter movies. Will the infamous Scottish wet weather dampen the spirits and scotch Rob’s chances of winning?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Vick Hope explore the chalk landscapes of the Chilterns, where rare grasslands, seasonal streams and specialised wildlife all depend on the fragile ground beneath their feet. But as habitats have been lost and broken into isolated fragments, some species have declined. Matt meets farmers working together to reconnect these landscapes, helps protect the endangered Duke of Burgundy butterfly and discovers how drone technology is transforming a chalkland vineyard. Vick visits a rare winterbourne stream that flows only after winter rains as restoration work helps bring it back to life. Meanwhile, Adam Henson welcomes a rare-breed middle white pig to his Cotswolds farm and trials crops that could cut fertiliser use.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: In this special episode of Deadly 60, Steve Backshall takes a deep dive into the fate of one of the most extraordinary, and endangered, ecosystems on our planet: coral reefs. They may cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, but they support roughly a quarter of all marine life and are irreplaceable - yet they are in serious trouble. Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. Along the way, he meets all the weird and wonderful creatures that call the reef home, including some of the best-camouflaged creatures and some impressive apex predators - he even gets a telling-off from a clownfish!

programme.title: Hey Duggee

But wait a minute... who is this unexpected guest in the big black car?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Everyone in Sweetwood has an itchy nose, itchy eyes or the sniffles, but they are not sick. Vida knows that something in Sweetwood is causing the symptoms and finally figures it out—flowers!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters spring into action when Glitch's mini-master toys invade Hong Kong Harbour.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Dash and Jake set off on a camping trip, determined to follow their wizarding scout rule: stick to the plan and use wits, not wishes. The family soon realise the original plan won’t work, but with teamwork, flexibility and one carefully chosen wish, Rafi helps turn a tricky situation into an exciting, new adventure. She learns that plans don’t have to be perfect, and sometimes changing them leads to something even better.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee’s precious clockwork music box breaks, her garden friends cheer her up with a life-size clockwork performance of their own.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s a hot day, so Justin and his friends cool off by visiting an ice cream farm. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble tries to keep Spotty cool but can’t seem to control his hosepipe!

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Nigel, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Layla, Maisy, Chester and Francis, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a wooden triangle toy, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by shapes. This theme is explored through play, song and story. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate shapes toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler. Storytime is all about discovering new words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear look for lots of different shapes at home and when they’re out and about. Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the shapes theme too. Plus, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri sings a song about how wonderful it is to have your very own body.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Cherry launches 'Cherry’s News' using a giant speaker, but she has nothing to say - and no-one brings her news. She doesn’t know that everyone in Fine Forest, including the Piggies, need help!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Amanpreet and Mum make delicious pakora together for a special family meal to celebrate Vaisakhi. They set the table and exchange beautiful Vaisakhi cards with Dad, but what will everyone think of Amanpreet’s fabulous feast? Later, Amanpreet and Mum get crafty and paint portraits of each other. Mum’s a bit nervous, but artist Amanpreet encourages her to show her creative side.

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Myrtle has a conference, so Stan becomes mayor for the day. Sophie and Benjamin are at hand to help.

programme.title: The Game Catchers

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Spring brings pollen, which makes the Tomatodons sneeze. Ginger and the Pea-Rexes must wrangle them across the tundra.

programme.title: Colourblocks

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are playing hide-and-seek. Murphi is so difficult to find that he comes out of hiding to help Rebecca make a cardboard tube tracker dog. The Mini Monsters make paper bag monsters, and Rebecca’s Grandpa calls to share his fishing frustrations. The Recycling Express brings a shoebox, inspiring a mega monster idea - a magnificent monster! And the Tiny Helpers are on hand to help make the hutch.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why beetles are important creatures to have in our outdoor spaces. They make a beetle habitat using an old bucket, some sticks and logs, and then they dig a big hole before planting it in a flower bed for beetles to visit.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Jen is doing a study of all the plants on Dino Island and has asked Andy to take photos of some of the rare plant specimens. While photographing them, Andy discovers unusual markings on some of the trees. With Jen’s help, he sets out to discover what’s making them and reveals an unlikely dinosaur culprit. Along the way, he meets a herd of Pachycephalosaurus and watches two males headbutting each other in a show of dominance.

programme.title: Supertato

Supertato spots the Cobs sabotaging the show, and when Evil Pea thinks she’s won the speedboat, she can’t get away because Supertato is holding it above his head!

programme.desc: Ginger joins the baby Pea-Rexes on their expedition to find dinner.

programme.desc: After Popcorn runs on his hamster wheel all night, he’s cranky the next day. Will he nap?

programme.desc: A strange rock far away from the ship breaks D.O.R.I.S.’s satnav. Luckily, Big Lizard’s on hand to teach Cosima how to find her way around without technology.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard

When the plate smashes a second time, Rafi wishes for help and summons the clumsy Fixie Pixie, who causes chaos while trying to repair things. Rafi eventually realises it’s better to tell the truth than hide mistakes.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran get caught in the rain at the park. They shelter under the bandstand and JoJo spots a rainbow! JoJo discovers that rainbows are only visible when it's rainy and sunny at the same time. On the way home, JoJo realises that rainbow colours are all around them, which inspires Gran Gran to have a plan - they can create their own rainbow at home!

Mum gives her a seed, and Lola can't help but imagine what her seed might grow into - a biscuit plant, a butterfly plant or maybe even a singing plant! Charlie shows her that first of all she has to learn to look after her plant.

programme.desc: Colly Wobble’s friends give her special things to pack into her toy suitcase. Colly Wobble takes her suitcase on a journey in Storyland, and each time she opens the suitcase, the special things make her think of her friends.

programme.desc: It’s the hottest day of the year, but Small wants it to snow. Paddie the polar bear visits the cafe, Small flies off to see how chocolate buttons are made, and the two friends make chilly polar cones for their Arctic guest.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to an old castle. On the way, they explore the rocky beach, go through a magic archway, walk like crabs and even see a pirate!

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: On Big Fix Day, Ava’s Good-As-New machine repairs everything - even things that don’t need mending. But when it fails, she has to find another way to fix the children’s toys.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels had a great adventure outside and want to tell everyone about it. What better way to tell a story than through a puppet show? First they make the puppets, using scissors, card, glue, glitter and feathers. Then it's time for an amazing show for all their friends! But wait a minute... who is this unexpected guest in the big black car?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Everyone in Sweetwood has an itchy nose, itchy eyes or the sniffles, but they are not sick. Vida knows that something in Sweetwood is causing the symptoms and finally figures it out—flowers!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters spring into action when Glitch's mini-master toys invade Hong Kong Harbour.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Dash and Jake set off on a camping trip, determined to follow their wizarding scout rule: stick to the plan and use wits, not wishes. The family soon realise the original plan won’t work, but with teamwork, flexibility and one carefully chosen wish, Rafi helps turn a tricky situation into an exciting, new adventure. She learns that plans don’t have to be perfect, and sometimes changing them leads to something even better.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee’s precious clockwork music box breaks, her garden friends cheer her up with a life-size clockwork performance of their own.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Parsnip performing a jaw-dropping escape that would leave even Houdini speechless.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s a hot day, so Justin and his friends cool off by visiting an ice cream farm. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble tries to keep Spotty cool but can’t seem to control his hosepipe!

programme.title: The Toddler Club
programme.desc: Nigel, Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear welcome toddlers Layla, Maisy, Chester and Francis, and their grown-ups, to the Toddler Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! The What’s in the Box? game reveals a wooden triangle toy, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by shapes. This theme is explored through play, song and story. Grown-ups are encouraged to take part at home by hiding a safe, toddler-appropriate shapes toy or object inside a recycled box for them to reveal and explore with their toddler. Storytime is all about discovering new words, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear look for lots of different shapes at home and when they’re out and about. Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the shapes theme too. Plus, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri sings a song about how wonderful it is to have your very own body.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Cherry launches 'Cherry’s News' using a giant speaker, but she has nothing to say - and no-one brings her news. She doesn’t know that everyone in Fine Forest, including the Piggies, need help!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Amanpreet and Mum make delicious pakora together for a special family meal to celebrate Vaisakhi. They set the table and exchange beautiful Vaisakhi cards with Dad, but what will everyone think of Amanpreet’s fabulous feast? Later, Amanpreet and Mum get crafty and paint portraits of each other. Mum’s a bit nervous, but artist Amanpreet encourages her to show her creative side.

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Myrtle has a conference, so Stan becomes mayor for the day. Sophie and Benjamin are at hand to help.

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers land on a very sensitive planet that tickles when you walk on it! They learn to play trowers and targets. But first, they need to work together to create some new, special socks.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Spring brings pollen, which makes the Tomatodons sneeze. Ginger and the Pea-Rexes must wrangle them across the tundra.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Cool Blue arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour blue

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are playing hide-and-seek. Murphi is so difficult to find that he comes out of hiding to help Rebecca make a cardboard tube tracker dog. The Mini Monsters make paper bag monsters, and Rebecca’s Grandpa calls to share his fishing frustrations. The Recycling Express brings a shoebox, inspiring a mega monster idea - a magnificent monster! And the Tiny Helpers are on hand to help make the hutch.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Thinking she is secretly one of the Peak City Heroes, the Rakoonz capture Becca.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers learn why beetles are important creatures to have in our outdoor spaces. They make a beetle habitat using an old bucket, some sticks and logs, and then they dig a big hole before planting it in a flower bed for beetles to visit.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Jen is doing a study of all the plants on Dino Island and has asked Andy to take photos of some of the rare plant specimens. While photographing them, Andy discovers unusual markings on some of the trees. With Jen’s help, he sets out to discover what’s making them and reveals an unlikely dinosaur culprit. Along the way, he meets a herd of Pachycephalosaurus and watches two males headbutting each other in a show of dominance.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It’s Banana's Big Supermarket Game Show, and Supertato is going head-to-head with Evil Pea to win a speedboat. But after failing in the first round, Evil Pea decides to get the Cobs to help her cheat. Supertato spots the Cobs sabotaging the show, and when Evil Pea thinks she’s won the speedboat, she can’t get away because Supertato is holding it above his head!

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and a group of children make pretend cakes, learn British Sign Language signs for pat, cake and baby, and sing and sign the rhyme Pat-a-Cake.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger joins the baby Pea-Rexes on their expedition to find dinner.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Norman is scared of the dark and can't get to sleep. Can Nick and the Popcasters find a song to help him snuggle down?

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: After Popcorn runs on his hamster wheel all night, he’s cranky the next day. Will he nap?

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: A strange rock far away from the ship breaks D.O.R.I.S.’s satnav. Luckily, Big Lizard’s on hand to teach Cosima how to find her way around without technology.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: It’s raining, so Rafi and Ruby are playing indoor football. But when they accidentally break a plate, Rafi wishes for it to be fixed but warns them not to play again. When the plate smashes a second time, Rafi wishes for help and summons the clumsy Fixie Pixie, who causes chaos while trying to repair things. Rafi eventually realises it’s better to tell the truth than hide mistakes.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran get caught in the rain at the park. They shelter under the bandstand and JoJo spots a rainbow! JoJo discovers that rainbows are only visible when it's rainy and sunny at the same time. On the way home, JoJo realises that rainbow colours are all around them, which inspires Gran Gran to have a plan - they can create their own rainbow at home!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. When Bread Man needs help, Sarah and Duck come to the rescue with their tandem bike!

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Charlie loves his little sister Lola, even if her imagination carries her away sometimes! Charlie is growing a tomato plant, and Lola wants to grow something too. Mum gives her a seed, and Lola can't help but imagine what her seed might grow into - a biscuit plant, a butterfly plant or maybe even a singing plant! Charlie shows her that first of all she has to learn to look after her plant.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Colly Wobble’s friends give her special things to pack into her toy suitcase. Colly Wobble takes her suitcase on a journey in Storyland, and each time she opens the suitcase, the special things make her think of her friends.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo takes care not to overfill a cup with water and teaches BaBa how to take sips from a very full drink. On the Play Tree, they fill containers with sand to make sandcastles. With the Yummies, they enjoy a delicious potato dish, which is very filling. As they sail on the Lullaby Lake, Elewhale fills the sky with twinkling stars. Gramma Leeba tells the friends about their very full day.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. The Tombliboos are playing inside when they hear something outdoors. It is the ball. Ooo collects the ball and brings it inside. The Tombliboos play with the ball indoors until it flies out of the window.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Join Perrie for a soothing story about the shapes that make up the world we love.

She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.title: Mamma Mia!
programme.desc: Romantic musical comedy. An independent single mother who owns a small hotel on the idyllic Greek isle of Kalokairi, Donna is about to let go of Sophie, the spirited daughter she's raised alone. Donna has invited her two life-long best girlfriends - practical, no-nonsense Rosie and wealthy multi-divorcee Tanya - from her one-time backing band Donna and the Dynamos for Sophie's wedding... and Sophie has secretly invited three guests of her own in a quest to find the identity of her father. To walk her down the aisle, Sophie brings back three men from Donna's past to the Mediterranean paradise that they visited 20 years earlier - new love will bloom and old romances will rekindle over 24 hours on a lush island full of possibilities... and the whole story is told through the music of ABBA.

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. After a night clubbing in central London with her friend Frankie, an exhausted Sarah is put into a black cab driven by John Worboys. Worboys engages her in friendly conversation before offering her champagne to celebrate a fictional casino win. Sarah reluctantly accepts, then passes out. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. After a night clubbing in central London with her friend Frankie, an exhausted Sarah is put into a black cab driven by John Worboys. Worboys engages her in friendly conversation before offering her champagne to celebrate a fictional casino win. Sarah reluctantly accepts, then passes out. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.title: Mamma Mia!
programme.desc: Romantic musical comedy. An independent single mother who owns a small hotel on the idyllic Greek isle of Kalokairi, Donna is about to let go of Sophie, the spirited daughter she's raised alone. Donna has invited her two life-long best girlfriends - practical, no-nonsense Rosie and wealthy multi-divorcee Tanya - from her one-time backing band Donna and the Dynamos for Sophie's wedding... and Sophie has secretly invited three guests of her own in a quest to find the identity of her father. To walk her down the aisle, Sophie brings back three men from Donna's past to the Mediterranean paradise that they visited 20 years earlier - new love will bloom and old romances will rekindle over 24 hours on a lush island full of possibilities... and the whole story is told through the music of ABBA.

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. After a night clubbing in central London with her friend Frankie, an exhausted Sarah is put into a black cab driven by John Worboys. Worboys engages her in friendly conversation before offering her champagne to celebrate a fictional casino win. Sarah reluctantly accepts, then passes out. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. Later, the households face their next immunity challenge, 'Escape the Greenhouse'. Who will secure safety at a crucial point in the competition? At the removal, Graham's shocking twist throws the neighbours into chaos, breaking bonds and burning bridges. Can any friendships come out unscathed?

programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.desc: The first episode of a comedy series providing an honest, uplifting and heart-warming portrayal of the lives of working-class teenagers from Liverpool while tackling issues with a refreshing humour. Recently-orphaned Southerner Christopher goes to live with his nan on a council estate in Liverpool - there he forms an unlikely unholy alliance with working-class Reece. On the verge of being expelled, Reece convinces his school's headmaster to give him one last chance and allow him to mentor Christopher to prove that he can positively contribute to the school - despite their differences, a friendship develops between the pair until Christopher throws Reece under the bus in order to impress a girl. An angry Reece can't resist getting his revenge on Christopher, but will this ruin his chances of remaining at the school? Meanwhile, Aimee reluctantly gives her boyfriend Lewis a gift to help with his sexual needs, but she soon learns that he has been cheating on her and seeks revenge...

programme.title: The Tower
programme.desc: Crime thriller. The death of working girl Lexi, who was murdered by Shakiel in revenge for Spencer's stabbing, sends shockwaves through Sarah's investigation and Operation Perseus - elsewhere, Kieran is already under pressure because wife Mary has thrown him out of their home and now faces an angry Lizzie who is demanding that he share information about Lexi with Sarah. However, Kieran is adamant that sharing information would not only alert Shakiel Oliver to the existence of Operation Perseus but would endanger Steve's life too - the pressure on Kieran then gets worse when his wife contacts Sarah and says that she has information about the Portland Tower case.

programme.desc: Your daily escape designed to calm the mind and encourage relaxation and reflection. [S,HD]

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton joins much-loved pets and their devoted owners behind the scenes at The Grove Vets, a busy family practice in the suburbs of Bristol run by husband-and-wife team Andy and Amy Valencia - this episode sees Fern meet Bailey, a lovable senior Labrador with a puzzling limp, while vet Dr James Greenwood examines 11-year-old Bamboo, the oldest rabbit on the practice's books. Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.

programme.desc: Proud Bristolian Josie Gibson takes us on a tour of her beloved West Country in a journey of celebration to discover dinner delights, freshly-caught lunches, the best of passionate artisan makers and growers and a few hidden gems to surprise us all - in this episode, Josie travels to the Jurassic Coast and tries her hand at the unique sport of Dorset knob-throwing. programme.desc: Britain's Got Talent goes live on Saturday nights for the Semi-Finals. In each week's show, a fresh variety of acts who impressed the judges during the auditions will put on exciting new performances as they compete for a place in the grand finale, getting one step closer to the life-changing prize of 250,000 pounds and a place on the bill of the Royal Variety Performance. Viewers at home hold the power to vote for their favourite acts of the night to send through to the ultimate stage of the competition, and the judges have their Golden Buzzer that can reward outstanding performers a ticket straight through to the live final.

programme.title: Mamma Mia!
programme.desc: Romantic musical comedy. An independent single mother who owns a small hotel on the idyllic Greek isle of Kalokairi, Donna is about to let go of Sophie, the spirited daughter she's raised alone. Donna has invited her two life-long best girlfriends - practical, no-nonsense Rosie and wealthy multi-divorcee Tanya - from her one-time backing band Donna and the Dynamos for Sophie's wedding... and Sophie has secretly invited three guests of her own in a quest to find the identity of her father. To walk her down the aisle, Sophie brings back three men from Donna's past to the Mediterranean paradise that they visited 20 years earlier - new love will bloom and old romances will rekindle over 24 hours on a lush island full of possibilities... and the whole story is told through the music of ABBA.

programme.title: Believe Me
programme.desc: In 2003, Sarah Adams is on her first night out since giving birth to her son, Jack. After a night clubbing in central London with her friend Frankie, an exhausted Sarah is put into a black cab driven by John Worboys. Worboys engages her in friendly conversation before offering her champagne to celebrate a fictional casino win. Sarah reluctantly accepts, then passes out. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Set in the heart of The Peak District, six households from across the UK move into a 'picture-perfect' village to compete for a massive £250,000 prize. As the close wave goodbye to another household, the competition ramps up in the final stages of the game. Giving the neighbours a chance to bond, Graham puts on some communal activities, a life-drawing class and a game of rounders. Later, the households face their next immunity challenge, 'Escape the Greenhouse'. Who will secure safety at a crucial point in the competition? At the removal, Graham's shocking twist throws the neighbours into chaos, breaking bonds and burning bridges. Can any friendships come out unscathed?

Worboys engages her in friendly conversation before offering her champagne to celebrate a fictional casino win. Sarah reluctantly accepts, then passes out. She wakes up in hospital, certain she has been raped by the cab driver. She endures the invasive examinations and relentless questioning that follow a rape report. The police, however, seem dismissive, focusing on the alcohol and small amount of cocaine Sarah had admitted to consuming, and questioning the plausibility of a rapist voluntarily driving his victim to a police station. After months of feeling unheard, her case is dropped, leaving Worboys free to continue his attacks.

Fern also scrubs up for surgery with skilled veterinary surgeon Andy, who is performing a laparoscopic keyhole spay operation on exuberant Hungarian Vizsla Etty, and celebrates the everyday heroes giving rescue dogs a fresh start with a visit to a Bristol dog sanctuary - we also meet owner Molly Rose, who has given former racing greyhound Flossie a second chance at life as she trains to be a therapy dog.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James heads east and travels to the region of Jura, where local farmer Matthew Tissot shows James around his beautiful orchard and teaches him about the region's remarkable apples and pears - James then barbecues duck accompanied by a spicy apple and pear chutney using fruit from Matthew's orchard. James then visits Fort des Rousses, which is home to one of France's most popular cheeses of comte, and is then cooked for by chef Jean-Paul Jeunet, who has been awarded two Michelin stars. Jean-Paul shares his take on a classic risotto using local ingredients - but in distinctly Swiss-looking surroundings - before James then cooks pork chops with Vichy-style carrots. When back home, James gives comfort food a decadent twist with his lobster mac and cheese and makes a warming apple tart.
